question.text: Indus Long-Short Fund (Cat III) is defending its 2.5x gross leverage to an LP DD team. The LP cites the LTCM case. The BEST Manager response, consistent with the Ch 12 leverage-risk framework, is:

answer.text: Under SEBI regulations, leverage risk in Cat III AIFs does not apply because Indian markets are well-regulated.
Our leverage is less than LTCM's 30:1 ratio so it is automatically safe.

Our leverage is within SEBI's prescribed maximum limits (2x of NAV for Cat III), we stress-test for convergence-trade risk and Russia-1998-style tail events, and we have pre-agreed deleveraging protocols.
LTCM was a USA fund with sovereign bond convergence trades, so it has no relevance to a long-short equity strategy.

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 12 Box 12.1 uses LTCM (30:1 leverage, USD 5bn equity on USD 125bn borrowings) to show how leverage + tail events destroyed the fund. SEBI prescribes max leverage for Cat III (2x of NAV). A credible Manager response acknowledges the regulatory cap, stress-test framework and deleveraging protocols. The Trap: A denies the risk. B is a relative-size fallacy. D dismisses a well-known LP teaching case. Cross-Exam Context: LTCM is a classic cross-exam topic (also in XV, XIX-B, XXI-B derivative/margin contexts). XIX-C Managers must own the lesson, not deflect. Manager's Pro-Tip: Have a one-page 'Leverage Playbook' citing SEBI's 2x NAV cap, your internal sub-cap (say 1.5x), daily margin monitoring, and deleveraging triggers. LPs love to see a pre-committed 'we will cut leverage if volatility exceeds X' protocol.
